clue.text: Delivery to many in the Yorkshire area

indicators.note: the letter for many sits inside the name of the Yorkshire area

parts.note: a Riding was one of the three old administrative divisions of Yorkshire
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A courier service drops off parcels to lots of households around Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically split into three Ridings (North, East and West), the source of the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridding is the act of freeing someone of something, so it is a deliverance or release.

clue.text: Half-cooked scrap of food

parts.note: meat that is only half-cooked is served rare
a scrap is a small bit

explanation.surface: Someone describes a morsel of underdone food on their plate.
explanation.walkthrough: RAREBIT is Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, a British savoury.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a dish of seasoned cheese sauce grilled on toast, so it is an example of a snack or meal.

clue.text: Reduction in total spending results in a flat

explanation.surface: An economist warns that cutting overall spending leaves things flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is playful: letting the air out of a tyre leaves you with a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: In economics the word means a fall in prices and demand from reduced spending; for a tyre, losing air leaves it flat.

clue.text: I prosecute student up for obstruction

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the following pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to prosecute someone is to sue them
L is the learner plate, a crossword stand-in for student

explanation.surface: Someone vows to bring a case against a student for blocking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SUE plus L into LEUS, which follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileus is a medical term for a blockage of the intestine, so it is a bowel obstruction.

clue.text: Fellow soundly digs his plot in the autumn

parts.note: a guy is a fellow, a chap

indicators.note: the word for what digs is said aloud to give a surname

parts.note: a garden fork digs, so digs gives forks

explanation.surface: A man gardening in autumn digs his allotment plot thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' signals that FORKS is said aloud as FAWKES (in a non-rhotic British accent). Guy Fawkes's Gunpowder Plot of November 1605 is remembered every autumn on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunpowder Plot conspirator is burned in effigy each November, so the November plot is linked to his name.

clue.text: Your uncle's steered the toboggan

parts.note: the British catchphrase 'Bob's your uncle' lets Your uncle's stand for Bob's
to have steered is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone's uncle guided the toboggan down the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob's your uncle' is a British expression meaning 'and there you have it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobsled is a racing sledge, a kind of toboggan used on ice runs.

clue.text: Taxi not available to turn up for this writer

indicators.note: in a down entry, to turn up means the joined pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
a flat no means something is not available

explanation.surface: A writer complains no taxi was free to come and collect him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses CAB plus NO, giving BAC then ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English essayist and philosopher, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Engagement as apprentice to the bar, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the following letters as only one possible arrangement

parts.note: L is the learner plate, so an apprentice is L

explanation.surface: A young law student is called to the Bar as a junior barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TOTHEBAR into BETROTHA, and L comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a formal promise to marry, the same thing as an engagement.

clue.text: She loves almost all the French race

indicators.note: almost all means the last letter of the race's name is dropped

parts.note: the Le Mans 24-hour race is held in France

explanation.surface: A woman adores nearly everything about the famous French motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Mans is the famous French 24-hour motor race; 'almost all' drops its S. LEMAN is an old word for a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A leman is an archaic word for a lover or mistress, a woman who loves someone.

clue.text: He's in the ballet, and sure to pirouette

indicators.note: a pirouette is a spin, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A male dancer is in the ballet and certain to spin on one foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pirouette' rearranges ANDSURE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, the man who performs in a ballet.

clue.text: Weapon in sack

explanation.surface: A gun is stashed inside a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a gun; to rifle is to ransack or plunder a place.

clue.text: Why, they say, maths can confuse a sailor

indicators.note: they say signals that the word why is said aloud as a letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

indicators.note: to confuse letters is to jumble them

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why arithmetic can baffle a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns WHY into Y by sound; 'confuse' rearranges MATHSCAN into ACHTSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman sails yachts, so he is a kind of sailor.

clue.text: This disciplinary officer's chair is suspended

definitions.text: This disciplinary officer's chair is suspended

parts.words: This disciplinary officer's chair is suspended
parts.note: a ship's petty officer in charge of crew and rigging gives his name to a seat slung from a rope

explanation.surface: An officer in charge of discipline has had his seat taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspended' suggests a punishment, but a bosun's chair is literally hung on a rope for working aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosun of a ship oversees the deck crew, and a bosun's chair is a seat hung from a line.

clue.text: Animal without the initiative to swoop

indicators.note: the initiative is the initial letter, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: to swoop on prey is to pounce

explanation.surface: A predator lacks the drive to swoop down on its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without the initiative' removes P, the initial letter of POUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: Old Germany city judge

explanation.surface: A judge from an old German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is an ancient city in western Germany founded by the Romans; a trier is one who tries a case.

clue.text: Draw attention, say, to mistake, and set to rights

indicators.note: say signals that the word for draw attention is spoken aloud

parts.note: to refer to something is to draw attention to it
bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone points out an error and corrects it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives REFUR from REFER spoken aloud. BISH is old British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To refurbish is to renovate or repair, putting something back in good order.

clue.text: He had an order to cook for the Field Marshal

definitions.text: He had an order to cook

explanation.surface: A chef was ordered to prepare food for the Field Marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was the British Field Marshal on the famous First World War recruiting poster, and a holder of several orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchener is a kitchen worker or cook; Lord Kitchener was a British Field Marshal.

clue.text: Courageous worker has a struggle — it started with a seizure

parts.note: one who works like a Trojan toils bravely and hard
a war is a struggle

explanation.surface: A brave employee battles on after a medical seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'seizure' is no fit but the abduction of Helen of Troy, which began the Greek legend's ten-year war.
explanation.definitionFit: The war of Greek legend began when Paris carried Helen off to Troy, an abduction or capture.

clue.text: The Owl makes Sir lose his head over a lark, say

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second
the knight loses his head, meaning the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
a lark is an example of a bird

explanation.surface: An owl causes a knight to panic over a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose his head' drops K from KNIGHT, leaving NIGHT; 'over' puts it above BIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl hunts after dark, so it is a creature of the darkness.

clue.text: Nothing to show this is a policy declaration

parts.note: to manifest something is to show it
O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A party has nothing to show voters except a statement of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a joke about an empty programme; the pieces go MANIFEST then O.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published statement of a party's aims and policies.

clue.text: Ghastly movie camera captures the bishop

indicators.note: the rearranged letters capture the bishop, holding it inside
movie is read as moving, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A gruesome film shows a cine camera catching the bishop on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movie' rearranges CAMERA into MACARE; 'captures' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome or grimly horrible, dwelling on death.

clue.text: Lines about the great period, in retrospect, of jurisprudence

indicators.note: the lines go about, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: L is short for line, so two make lines

indicators.note: looking back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: an age is a great period of time

explanation.surface: Lines about a past golden era of law, looked back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns AGE into EGA; 'about' puts LL around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means relating to the law, so it describes matters of jurisprudence.

clue.text: Leaner breed of hunting dog

explanation.surface: A slimmer kind of hound used for hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: A LURCHER is a British crossbred hunting dog, part sighthound.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lurches sways or leans over; a lurcher is a crossbred hound kept for hunting.

clue.text: It has branches in Lebanon

parts.note: reads like a company with offices in Lebanon, but means a tree that grows there

explanation.surface: A firm has offices in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' suggests a bank or a chain store; the tree is on Lebanon's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar of Lebanon is a coniferous tree that is the national emblem of the country.

clue.text: Look for water to plunge into

explanation.surface: Searching for water to dive into.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground springs with a rod; it is also a spelling of douse, to dip in liquid.

clue.text: The killing of animals thus large is a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a mess, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Culling animals on so great a scale is a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a disaster' rearranges THUSLARGE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is the butchering of livestock for food.

clue.text: Chair in American saloon

explanation.surface: A seat inside a bar in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a saloon is a car with a separate boot, which Americans call a sedan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles; a sedan is the American word for a saloon car.

clue.text: Gadget for soldier's doctor

parts.note: GI is an American soldier, so soldier's is GI's
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A device made for an army man's physician.
explanation.walkthrough: MO stands for Medical Officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo, also spelt gizmo, is any clever gadget or device.

clue.text: The curve of the bay is obvious here

definitions.text: The curve of the bay is obvious here

parts.words: The curve of the bay is obvious here
parts.note: sounds like a coastline, but the bay is a projecting window and its curve shows in the shape

explanation.surface: A coastal view where the sweep of the bay is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests the coast; it is a bay window, and a curved one is named for its bowed shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved bay window projecting from a wall in an arc is named for that bowed shape.

clue.text: "Chuck it, _____" (Chesterton)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the refrain of G. K. Chesterton's poem mocking the politician F. E. ...

explanation.surface: A line of verse with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton's poem 'Antichrist, or the Reunion of Christendom' ends each verse with this refrain, aimed at F. E. Smith, later Lord Birkenhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The refrain addresses the British politician F. E. Smith by his surname, which completes the quotation.

clue.text: Butler twice visited this resort

parts.note: reads like a servant's holidays, but means the novelist Samuel Butler wrote about a utopian land and then its sequel

explanation.surface: A manservant has holidayed at the same seaside town two times.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Butler wrote a satirical novel of that title (1872) and its sequel, '... Revisited' (1901); 'Butler' pretends to be a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the imaginary country of Samuel Butler's satire, whose name is nowhere spelt backwards.

clue.text: Have to ask again from failure, or dereliction

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken straight out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone must ask again after a failure or neglect of duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'failure', 'or' and 'dereliction'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to place an order again, asking a second time for goods.
